CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while at a trampoline park with his wife. This was his first visit to a trampoline park, engaged in recreational jumping. He heard a snap and experienced immediate pain on the lateral aspect of the right knee. He took acetaminophen which provided no relief. He elevated the knee but did not use ice or heat. He denies a regular exercise routine and reports this was recreational activity. He has tolerated the pain for one week before presenting to clinic.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Musculoskeletal: Right knee pain, lateral aspect, with difficulty ambulating; has a limp and can bear weight but with difficulty. Able to bend and straighten knee with pain. All other systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not obtained.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is married. Engages in occasional recreational activities. Reports inconsistent exercise routine. Diet consists of general observation with attention to carbohydrate monitoring, no specific calorie counting or structured diet. Denies keto diet or low salt diet. Does not like to come to doctors. Does not have a home blood pressure cuff.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure elevated at approximately 180/80 mmHg.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Right knee with mild tenderness on palpation of lateral aspect, no tenderness on medial aspect. Good range of motion with ability to bend and straighten knee. Able to bear weight with limp noted. Ecchymosis and edema present along lateral aspect. No effusion. Gait demonstrates slight limp.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - Lateral ligament strain
   - Start meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling
   - Refer to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention
   - Expected to heal on its own; consider further imaging if pain persists

2. Hypertension
   - Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily
   - Order transthoracic echocardiogram given suboptimal blood pressure control
   - Consider medication modification based on results

3. Diabetes mellitus
   - Order hemoglobin A1C to assess long-term glycemic control
   - Order lipid panel for potential medication adjustments
